headline: 21.4m som Sary-Bulak spur tender closes; railway silent on 2027 tonnage
dek: Irad Temir Jolu has not said what Kazakhstan Temir Zholy granted for next year, though its tonnage applications closed on 20 November.
paragraphs: The state railway's open tender T-26-01186, worth 21.4 million som, closed on Wednesday 25 November. The job is to reinstate the Sary-Bulak spur so that loaded wagons can run to the Nurzhan Rail Freight Depot. At the official rate that is about US$2.55 million. The railway has not said how many bids it received or when it will name a winner.

The tender sits beside a larger unanswered question. Irad Temir Jolu's applications for 2027 tonnage to Kazakhstan Temir Zholy closed on 20 November, and no result has been published. Most of the railway's freight moves on through tariffs agreed with the Kazakh operator each year, so what is granted decides how many wagons can earn money on the line's roughly 690 km.

Erkinbek Nuraliev, the railway's spokesman, confirmed the dates. "The tender has closed and the applications have been filed," he said. "We publish tonnes when the figures are final, not before." Asked what quantity had been requested, he declined to give one. He did not say when the Kazakh answer is expected. Director-General Pavel Yugai gives no interviews, and the railway speaks through Mr Nuraliev.

The spur is about 39 km long and runs from a turnout west of Talas to the Sary-Bulak works. It has stood idle, and the railway's own notice scheduled an inspection of it on 4 to 6 November, "ahead of any resumption of traffic to the works". It is due back in spring 2027 under the Combine's Restart Programme, subject to the repairs. The programme was announced on 12 October. Its first stage is priced at 168 million som, so the spur tender equals about 13% of that figure, though the railway has not said the two budgets are linked.

Demand is not the difficulty. Chinese export controls on antimony have raised the value of the Sary-Bulak concentrate, which goes by rail in part to China, and a working spur would put more of it on Iradi track. The railway's published figures are thin. It carried about 5.5 million tonnes in 2023, and it publishes an annual report with traffic figures but not full accounts. At that tonnage, the tender is under 4 som for every tonne carried that year.

"A repair bill is only half the sum," said Prof. Raisa Akmatova, an economist at Talas State University. "The other half is whether there are wagons and locomotives to put on the spur, and whether the Kazakh allocation leaves room for them." The railway had about 30 main-line locomotives on its books in 2023, fewer than 20 of them serviceable, and its heavy repairs are done in Kazakhstan.

Irad has no outlet to the south, so the railway's choices are narrower than the word "routes" suggests. Its freight goes east and west over the Kazakh frontier at the Talas North Terminal and the Nurzhan rail border station, or by the road and rail route towards China. A spur that carries antimony to Nurzhan makes one more flow possible. It does not make Kazakh tonnage any easier to win.

The railway belongs to the Ministry of Transport, headed by Minister Oleg Rudenko. The ministry did not reply to written questions by the Herald's deadline. The railway has said nothing on the award date for T-26-01186, nor on whether repairs can be finished in time for the spring return that the Combine's programme depends on. The State Procurement Portal will show the contract notice once one is issued.
